memory_candidates.content: When wiring a shared behavioral contract into multiple self-contained sibling agent files (e.g. lean/cslib hard agents that intentionally do not @-reference each other), lock the exact Context References bullet + inline internalization block text once (e.g. in the plan's working notes), paste it verbatim into every consumer, then verify drift with md5sum on the extracted section across all files before marking the wiring phase complete.

Extension-local agents (e.g. .claude/extensions/{ext}/agents/*.md) deploy to .claude/agents/ via symlinks for some extensions (cslib) but may be entirely absent from .claude/agents/ for others (lean, observed in this repo) -- always verify actual symlink/deployment state with `ls -la .claude/agents/` and `readlink -f` before assuming a canonical-source edit will reach the deployed agent; edit the canonical extension source regardless, since that is authoritative.

Extensions consumed by a separate repo (e.g. /home/benjamin/Projects/cslib consuming .claude/extensions/lean and .claude/extensions/cslib) use file-copy installation via .claude/scripts/install-extension.sh, not a live link -- any edit to shared extension context/agents/index-entries.json in the authoring repo requires a manual re-run of install-extension.sh inside each consuming repo to propagate; this must be explicitly flagged in the implementation summary/handoff rather than assumed to sync automatically.
